items.title: Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, stock soars; Anthropic slides
items.summary: The 8:30 team is joined by Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit to discuss why washed-out sentiment doesn't mean a fundamental bottom, his $50-to-$250 bull-bear range on Anthropic, and how to handicap the "Jensen premium" coming back into Nvidia. Deirdre Bosa Live host Deirdre Bosa also joins to break down Silicon Valley's reaction to Huang's return and what it means for the AI trade.

items.title: Smith + Nephew names new CFO
items.summary: Nick Alexos will join the orthopedics company later this month after holding CFO roles at Univar Solutions and Dentsply Sirona.

items.title: Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR) Partners With Apollo, Is It Still A Bargain?
items.summary: Victory Capital Holdings (VCTR) just moved to deepen its product lineup, announcing a collaboration with Apollo Global Management that combines Apollo’s private markets expertise with Victory’s public markets and distribution reach. items.title: SpaceX Is Paying Up to 8.36% on $44 Billion of Debt for Nvidia Chips
items.summary: Lenders lined up to fund SpaceX's chip spree, then demanded a steep price for it. The real risk may be what happens to those GPUs, and to SpaceX's cash flow, before the first rent check clears.

items.title: Apollo (APO) Stock May Be 30% Undervalued As AI Credit Risks Loom
items.summary: Apollo Global Management has delivered a 70.4% total return over the past 5 years, yet the recent share price pullback and fresh deal activity put a sharper spotlight on whether that valuation can be explained by the returns it earns on its capital. A 70.4% gain over 5 years puts real weight on the question of whether Apollo's current price is anchored in the actual profitability of the capital it deploys for clients and on its own balance sheet. items.title: SpaceX Sells $32 Bil Of Debt For AI Chips. But Yields, Orbital Deployment Raise Concerns.
items.summary: SpaceX sold $32 billion of debt to help fund AI chips, equipment. But concerns rise over high yields, orbital data center deployments.

items.title: Apollo views daily pricing as key to expanding alternatives access. Industry peers are skeptical.
items.summary: In the wake of several high-profile blowups in private credit, some managers have taken steps to improve transparency in an asset class known for its illiquidity and opacity. items.title: Apollo-backed insurer Athora weighs sale of Belgian unit, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: Investing.com -- Athora Holding Ltd., the European life insurer backed by Apollo Global Management (NYSE:APO), is exploring a potential sale of its Belgian operations as part of a broader effort to sharpen its geographic focus, according to reporting from Bloomberg. The insurer has enlisted advisers to gauge preliminary interest from prospective buyers, though discussions remain at an early stage and management could still elect to retain the division.
